newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed despite gold fall.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed despite gold fall.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Wednesday, after gold initially fell to fresh three year lows, as the US dollar surged higher, in the wake of an upbeat assessment of the US economy by Federal Reserve chairman Greenspan Tuesday.

"The hopeful point is that there wasn't any followthrough to the downside after gold tested $350, as the dollar surged higher encouraged by Greenspan," Chase Manhattan New York managing director Dinsa Mehta said.
"But the market is still short, with talk of South African hedging now the rand has begun to stabilize again."

COMEX February gold ended down $2.10 an ounce at $351.70, after seeing a new contract low in ACCESS trade overnight at $349.80, but most of the estimated total volume of 39,000 lots was seen in the morning session.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $350.50/00, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $351.20, and the New York close Tuesday at $352.70/20.

With the South African rand stabilizing, the price of gold in rand fell to fresh six month lows Wednesday, around 1617 rand, with some high cost South African producers now seen near break even level, analysts said.

Ongoing fears of more European central bank sales were highlighted by a report from Dutch bank, Rabobank, suggesting the Dutch central bank, Bank Nederlandsche, could sell a further 200 tonnes of gold, in addition to the 300 tonnes confirmed sold last week.

Meanwhile, commodity funds, which were carrying near record net short positions in the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report last Friday, look to be rolling their positions into forward months, analysts said.
The COMEX February/April gold spread narrowed further to $1.40 an ounce Wednesday from $1.60 Tuesday.
Open interest in COMEX February gold fell 4,260 lots Tuesday, in data released Wednesday, while April open interest jumped 4,767 lots.
Total COMEX gold open interest rose 3,280 lots to 204,471 lots.
Gold remained weaker than silver, with spot gold/silver ratio falling to near five month lows at 74.25.
COMEX March silver ended up 0.8 cent at $4.723 an ounce, after seeing a $4.690-4.745 range, on total estimated silver volume of 16,000 lots.
Gold was weaker than platinum also, with the COMEX April platinum/gold spread rising to $6.80 an ounce from $5.20 Tuesday.
Nevertheless, NYMEX April platinum saw a new life-of-contract low at $359.50, before ending down $1.70 at $359.80 an ounce.
NYMEX March palladium closed up five cents at $123.60.
